# Gravel God Race Database — Full Context

> 370 gravel, MTB, and bikepacking races rated on 14 base dimensions plus a Cultural Impact bonus.
> Produced by Gravel God (gravelgodcycling.com). Generated: 2026-07-25

## Scoring Methodology

Each race is scored on 14 base dimensions (1-5 scale):
logistics, length, technicality, elevation, climate, altitude, adventure, prestige, race_quality, experience, community, field_depth, value, expenses.
Cultural Impact is a bonus dimension scored from 0-5.

Overall score = round(((sum of 14 base scores + Cultural Impact) / 70) * 100).

Tier assignment:
- Tier 1 (Elite): score >= 80, OR prestige=5 + score>=75
- Tier 2 (Contender): score >= 60, OR prestige=5 + score<75 (capped at T2)
- Tier 3 (Solid): score >= 45
- Tier 4 (Roster): score < 45
- Prestige 4 promotes one tier (but not into T1)

## Tier 1 & Tier 2 Races (153 races)

### Transcontinental Race
Tier 1 | Score: 97/100 | 3100 mi | 210,000 ft | Across Europe (route changes annually) | July | bikepacking
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/transcontinental-race/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/transcontinental-race.md

The flagship European ultra — 4,000-5,000km self-supported across a continent. Mike Hall's legacy. The ultimate test of human endurance on a road bike. A continental crossing by bicycle. Start and finish points change each year — London to Istanbul, Geraardsbergen to Thessaloniki, Roubaix to Istanbul, Santiago de Compostela to Constanta, and Trondheim to Kalamata. The free-route format means riders plan their own path between 4 mandatory control points, each spaced 500-1,200km apart. Between checkpoints, you could ride 800km on flat highways or 600km through mountain passes — the strategic choice is yours. Mandatory parcours at each control point (5-100+ km of prescribed route, often on gravel through mountains) force every rider through the same crucible. The TCR is not about any single course — it is about the concept: cross Europe by bike, self-supported, as fast as you can. Signature challenge: 4,000-5,000km self-supported across a continent. Free-route navigation between mandatory control points. 30,000-64,000m climbing depending on edition and route choice. 0-40C temperature range. Clock never stops. No support. The ultimate test of human endurance, navigation, and self-reliance on a road bike. The Transcontinental Race is ultra-distance cycling's most iconic European event. Founded by Mike Hall in 2013, it established the template for self-supported racing that defines the sport. 4,000-5,000km across a continent, free-route format, clock never stops, completely self-supported. TCR does not compare to other races — it is the standard against which all European ultra races are measured. Finishing is a lifetime achievement. Winning is legend. Yes if you have 2+ years ultra-distance experience, can ride 300-400km days consistently, handle extreme sleep deprivation, and want cycling's ultimate European challenge. Yes if you have completed Paris-Brest-Paris, a 1,200km+ audax, or a shorter ultra-distance race. Skip if you have not completed multi-day unsupported rides. Skip if you cannot commit to 6+ months of dedicated training. Skip if you expect it to be 'just a long race' — this is an expedition that happens to be timed. Non-negotiables: Ultra-distance riding experience — minimum 1,200km+ unsupported ride completed; Proven equipment setup tested over 1,000+ km including charging system, lighting, and navigation; Route planning for all 4 checkpoint-to-checkpoint segments with contingency alternatives

### Tour Divide
Tier 1 | Score: 94/100 | 2745 mi | 200,000 ft | Banff, Alberta to Antelope Wells, New Mexico | June | bikepacking
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/tour-divide/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/tour-divide.md

The longest mountain bike time trial on earth—2,745 miles from Banff to Mexico, completely self-supported, pure amateur ethos. A 2,745-mile expedition along the Continental Divide from Canada to Mexico. The route passes through 5 US states and 2 Canadian provinces, crossing the Divide 30+ times. Terrain ranges from glaciated Canadian Rockies to Wyoming's Red Desert to Colorado's 11,000+ foot passes to New Mexico's rocky Gila Wilderness. Surface is roughly 90% unpaved—mostly gravel and forest service roads with some singletrack and paved connectors. The character changes daily as you ride south through changing ecosystems, elevations, and climates. Signature challenge: The complete package—2,745 miles of self-supported suffering through every climate zone, every terrain type, and every mental state across 2-4 weeks on the Continental Divide. Tour Divide is bikepacking racing at its purest and most extreme. 2,745 miles from Banff to Mexico, completely self-supported, no entry fee, no prizes, no sponsors—just you, your bike, and the Continental Divide for 2-4 weeks. It's not really comparable to other races; it's an expedition that happens to be timed. The combination of distance, elevation, terrain diversity, climate extremes, and complete self-reliance creates something unique in endurance sports. With only ~716 finishers in history and a 47-60% DNF rate, completing Tour Divide joins a very exclusive club. Yes if you have serious ultra-endurance experience and can commit 2-4 weeks to the Continental Divide. Yes if you can handle complete self-sufficiency across remote terrain. Yes if you want the ultimate test. Skip if you haven't completed multi-day self-supported events. Skip if you need race organization, aid stations, or support crews. Skip if you cannot repair your own bike.

### Unbound Gravel 200
Tier 1 | Score: 93/100 | 200 mi | 11,000 ft | Emporia, Kansas | May | gravel
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/unbound-200/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/unbound-200.md

The gravel race by which all others are measured. Relentless. Not one killer climb, but 200 miles of constant attrition. At 200 miles, this is a full-day effort. With 11K+ feet of climbing, the vertical gain is relentless. Signature challenge: The heat. The duration. The Flint Hills don't negotiate. Heat adaptation isn't optional—it's survival. The combination of 200 miles and extreme temperatures creates a unique endurance challenge. Unbound is gravel racing's Mount Everest—not because it's the hardest course, but because it's the race that defines the sport. Riders don't 'do' Unbound casually. They plan for it, obsess over heat protocols, and show up knowing that crossing the line in Emporia means something. The course itself isn't new—rolling terrain, gravel, heat. What makes it legendary is the field, the atmosphere, and the weight of the finish line. If you finish Unbound, you've earned it. If you're asking whether Unbound is 'worth it,' the answer is probably yes—but only if you're willing to commit to the training, the logistics, and the reality that this race will test every assumption you have about your durability. It's not fun. It's not easy. But it's unforgettable. Non-negotiables: Heat adaptation protocol built into weeks 6-10; Flint-specific cornering and line selection skills; 9-hour dress rehearsal in week 9

### The Traka 200
Tier 1 | Score: 91/100 | 126 mi | 8,694 ft | Girona, Catalonia, Spain | April | gravel
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/the-traka/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/the-traka.md

Europe's Unbound-distance race — 202km of technical Mediterranean gravel from Girona's Empordà plains to the Gavarres massif in a single day. A full day of Mediterranean gravel racing: a paved climb out of Girona opens the route before dropping onto gravel, the Empordà plains carry riders past olive groves and stone farmhouses toward Figueres, a long gentle climb runs from Anglès to Sant Hilari Sacalm, and a technical Gavarres massif singletrack finale closes the loop back into Girona. 84% unpaved, with rocky Mediterranean surfaces demanding real bike-handling in the closing kilometers. Signature challenge: The Gavarres massif singletrack finale — technical, demanding bike-handling, and saved for the closing kilometers back into Girona. If you're serious about gravel and have any connection to European cycling culture, the Traka 200 is a must. It's not just a race — it's a pilgrimage to the sport's spiritual home. Where else can you ride the same roads out of Girona that WorldTour pros train on, then finish through the Gavarres massif in a single day? Yes, if you want Europe's premier one-day gravel experience and can handle a full day of racing inside a 12-hour cutoff. The Traka 200 delivers Gravel Earth Series-level legitimacy, stunning Catalan terrain, and a genuinely international field. Just be ready for rocky, technical sections and pack tires suited to 84% unpaved ground.

### Colorado Trail Race
Tier 1 | Score: 90/100 | 530 mi | 72,500 ft | Durango to Denver, Colorado | August | bikepacking
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/colorado-trail-race/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/colorado-trail-race.md

The Colorado Trail doesn't care about your FTP when you're pushing your bike through talus fields at 13,000 feet. The CTR is 530 miles of high-altitude punishment disguised as a trail race. You'll spend most of your time above 10,000 feet, where 70% singletrack means constant technical riding interrupted by mandatory hike-a-bikes. This isn't gravel racing—it's Alpine survival with a bike occasionally underneath you. Signature challenge: The altitude never lets up—you'll average over 10,000 feet for 530 miles while navigating technical singletrack that forces constant hike-a-bikes. Most riders don't realize that CTR's difficulty isn't the climbing, it's maintaining any rhythm when you're pushing your bike every few miles at oxygen levels that make sea-level riders dizzy just standing still. This is for riders who've already proven they can suffer for days, not weekends. You need legitimate bikepacking experience, gear dialed for everything from desert heat to alpine storms, and the fitness to hike-a-bike for miles without breaking. If you haven't done multi-day self-supported racing or think 530 miles sounds doable because you can ride centuries, stay home.

### Trans Am Bike Race
Tier 1 | Score: 90/100 | 4233 mi | 175,000 ft | Astoria, Oregon to Yorktown, Virginia | June | bikepacking
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/trans-am-bike-race/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/trans-am-bike-race.md

The longest self-supported bike race on earth—4,200+ miles from Pacific to Atlantic, crossing 10 states, no support crews, pure transcontinental adventure. A 4,200+ mile expedition from Pacific to Atlantic following the historic TransAmerica Bicycle Trail. The route passes through 10 states, crossing the Continental Divide in Colorado and the Appalachian Mountains in Virginia. Surface is roughly 90% paved—quiet county roads, bike paths, and low-traffic highways. The character evolves dramatically: Pacific Northwest forests, Rocky Mountain passes, endless Kansas plains, Ozark rollercoasters, Ohio River farmland, and steep Appalachian ridges. This is America condensed into one transcontinental ride. Signature challenge: The complete American experience—4,200 miles coast to coast through every landscape, every climate, every mental state across 2-5 weeks of self-supported suffering. Trans Am Bike Race is the longest self-supported bike race on earth—4,200+ miles from the Pacific to Atlantic, completely self-supported, across 10 states and every American landscape. While Tour Divide claims the crown for toughest mountain bike ultra, Trans Am is the road equivalent: pure expedition cycling at maximum distance. The mostly-paved route is more accessible technically but no less demanding physically—175,000 feet of climbing over 2-5 weeks will humble any cyclist. With the historic TransAmerica Trail as its backbone and 50 years of trail angel culture, this is America's great cycling pilgrimage. Yes if you have serious ultra-endurance experience and can commit 2-5 weeks to crossing America. Yes if you can handle complete self-sufficiency across 4,200 miles. Yes if you want the ultimate American cycling pilgrimage. Skip if you haven't completed multi-day self-supported events. Skip if 200+ mile days for weeks on end sounds impossible. Skip if Kansas wind and Appalachian rollercoasters would break your spirit.

### UCI Gravel World Championships
Tier 1 | Score: 90/100 | 112 mi | 8,202 ft | Rotating (2024: Heerlen, Netherlands) | October | gravel
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/uci-gravel-worlds/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/uci-gravel-worlds.md

The only gravel race where you can actually call yourself World Champion—if you can handle 180km of whatever terrain the UCI throws at you. 180 km elite, 140 km age group. 70% gravel, 30% paved. Varies by location. Technical rating: 4/5. Signature challenge: 180 km elite + World Championship field + October weather. Rainbow jersey. UCI Gravel World Championships is World Championship—180 km elite, 140 km age group. Founded 2022. 70% gravel, 30% paved. Rotating locations (2022-2023 Italy, 2024 Netherlands). 1,000+ riders (elite + age group). October autumn conditions (10-20°C, 40% rain). UCI license required (€100-€150 / $110-$165). If you want World Championship rainbow jersey and fastest field in gravel, this is it. If you need domestic/local race, skip it. International destination, prestige 5. You need a UCI license, the fitness for nearly five hours of World Championship pace racing, and the mental fortitude to suffer in front of 1,000+ of the world's fastest gravel riders. The course changes annually, so you're gambling on terrain, but if you can't handle 2,500m of climbing and October weather in Europe, stay home. This isn't about participation—it's about proving you belong with the global elite.

### Unbound XL
Tier 1 | Score: 90/100 | 350 mi | 14,000 ft | Emporia, Kansas | May | gravel
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/unbound-xl/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/unbound-xl.md

The longest gravel race that matters, where the Flint Hills strip away everything but what's left of your soul. Unbound XL is a 350-mile commitment to Kansas limestone gravel that slices tires and punishes poor line choices across the rolling Flint Hills. The course feels like prairie purgatory — constant undulations that never let you settle into a rhythm, with long stretches between gas station salvation points. Sharp, chunky gravel demands constant vigilance while the relentless rollers chip away at your soul one hill at a time. Signature challenge: The 75-mile gap between meaningful resupply points turns nutrition into a high-stakes chess match. Most riders crack not from the hills or the gravel, but from running out of food or water in the Kansas void where gas stations close at 10 PM and your mistakes compound in the darkness. You need to finish a 200-miler first, preferably two. The 36-hour cutoff sounds generous until you're grinding limestone in your 16th hour with 150 miles still ahead. Self-supported means what it says—no crew, no checkpoints, just you and whatever gas stations stay open past midnight in rural Kansas.

Desert badlands that look like Mars, Europe's only true desert (Tabernas), and the 3,396m Pico Veleta climb. Self-supported means you carry what you need between remote villages. The combination of distance, elevation, heat, and self-reliance is unmatched in gravel racing. Signature challenge: The complete package—800km of desert heat, alpine altitude, and multi-day self-supported suffering through some of Europe's most extreme terrain. Badlands is gravel racing taken to its logical extreme. 800km, 16,000m climbing, 40°C+ deserts, 3,400m alpine passes, completely self-supported. It's not really comparable to other gravel races—it's an expedition that happens to be timed. The combination of distance, elevation, heat, and self-reliance creates something uniquely brutal. Finishing Badlands is a lifetime achievement that earns permanent respect in ultra-endurance circles. Yes if you have genuine ultra-endurance experience and want the ultimate test. Yes if you can handle extreme heat and self-support logistics. Skip if you haven't completed multi-day bikepacking events or can't adapt to 40°C+ conditions.

### Crusher in the Tushar
Tier 1 | Score: 89/100 | 69.9 mi | 10,000 ft | Beaver, Utah | July | gravel
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/crusher-in-the-tushar/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/crusher-in-the-tushar.md

The climber's gravel race—where thin air separates pretenders from contenders. Relentless vertical. You climb for 35 miles, then descend for 35 miles. Simple math, brutal execution. Signature challenge: The altitude. 10,000+ feet average means your power is down 10-15%. Plan accordingly. Crusher is what happens when you take a mountain stage of the Tour and add gravel. It's not for everyone—flat-landers and non-climbers will suffer disproportionately. But if you love vertical and want to test yourself against thin air, this is your race. If you love climbing and want a race that rewards it, absolutely. If you're a diesel-engine flat-lander, consider something else. The altitude alone makes this a specialist's race.

The mountain bike endurance race that defines the category. Bucket list for a reason. Out-and-back with one massive climb (Columbine) and relentless terrain. The altitude is the course. ### Belgian Waffle Ride
Tier 1 | Score: 87/100 | 107 mi | 7,367 ft | Del Mar, California | April | gravel
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/bwr-california/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/bwr-california.md

The race where bike handling skills outweigh FTP and 40% learn what DNF feels like. The 2026 Waffle starts and finishes at the Del Mar Polo Fields and covers 107 miles with 7,367 feet of climbing. Its 30 unroad sectors make up 53% of the route and mix gravel, deep sand, rocks, doubletrack, decomposed granite, dirt, and singletrack. The former Double Peak summit finish is not part of the Del Mar course; Zick-Zack and Saint Lusardi are among the closing sectors. Signature challenge: The un-road format—tire choice and bike handling matter as much as FTP—now closes with Zick-Zack and Saint Lusardi instead of the retired Double Peak summit finish. Belgian Waffle Ride earns its 'Hell of the North County' nickname through relentless variety rather than single massive climbs. The current-era course (Del Mar Polo Fields venue, since 2025) runs roughly 106-107 miles with about 7,500 feet of climbing, mixing 70% pavement with 30% 'unroad'—dirt, gravel, single-track, sand, water crossings, and rock gardens. Earlier editions (pre-2025, San Marcos venue) ran longer, 120-135 miles with 10,000+ feet of gain. Founder Michael Marckx designed the route to expose riders who rely on draft in group rides but lack comprehensive bike handling and endurance skills. The 40% DNF rate validates the course's effectiveness at separating technical riders from pure power athletes, maintaining BWR's identity as an 'un-road' race rather than a pure gravel endurance test. Yes, if you have legitimate technical skills from cyclocross or mountain biking, can handle 12+ hour moving time, and want to test yourself against a course designed to expose weaknesses. The race rewards actual bike riding—handling rough descents, choosing correct lines through sand, managing energy across varied terrain. It's expensive and honest about your capabilities. Skip it if you're purely a power athlete with limited technical skills, have never ridden extended single-track or sand, or can't stomach California travel costs ($1,200-1,800 total). Also skip if you need grassroots intimacy—BWR offers professional production and competitive intensity, not community warmth.

### Torino Nice Rally
Tier 1 | Score: 87/100 | 435 mi | 52,493 ft | Turin, Italy to Nice, France | September | bikepacking
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/torino-nice-rally/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/torino-nice-rally.md

The quintessential European bikepacking pilgrimage - 700km crossing the Alps on legendary military roads for 25 EUR. A 700km pilgrimage across the Maritime Alps from Turin's Piazza Giambattista Bodoni to Nice's Rifugio Massacan. The route weaves between Italy and France across 10+ major cols, alternating between legendary Tour de France climbs and historic military gravel roads. 65% paved alpine roads, 35% gravel including the sublime Gardetta Pass 'Little Peru' and Via del Sale finale. Every day takes riders over passes above 2,000m. The sweet spot between 2,000-3,000m where peaks escape trees and sky becomes more blue. Signature challenge: The complete Alpine crossing - 700km, 16,000m+ climbing, legendary military roads, self-supported through the Maritime Alps from Italy to France. The Torino Nice Rally represents bikepacking at its purest. 700km crossing the Maritime Alps from Italy to France on legendary military roads, fully self-supported, for 25 EUR. It's not a race - it's a pilgrimage. The Gardetta Pass 'Little Peru' section is described as possibly the most mesmerizing gravel ride in the world. Via del Sale's finale is 30km of dream gravel. The refugio culture, the rolling community, the charity mission for Smart Shelter Foundation - this is what the bikepacking ethos looks like when executed with soul. Founded with Tour Divide inspiration, TNR has earned its legendary status. Yes if you want authentic bikepacking adventure without commercial racing pressure. Yes if you appreciate community, charity, and soul over competition. Yes if you're prepared for multi-day Alpine self-sufficiency. Skip if you need race infrastructure and support. Skip if rocky military roads will destroy your pure gravel setup.

### Gravel Earth Series
Tier 1 | Score: 86/100 | 208 mi | 12,139 ft | Global (HQ: Girona, Spain) | February | gravel
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/gravel-earth/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/gravel-earth.md

Europe's premier gravel circuit—global adventure racing from Girona to Kenya to Iceland, built on passion over profit. A global circuit that delivers genuine adventure across continents. The Traka offers Mediterranean gravel with sea views and Catalan forest trails. Migration throws riders into Kenya's safari lands with wildlife encounters and Maasai villages. Iceland provides volcanic otherworldliness. The Oregon Trail delivers American multi-day stage racing. Each event is distinct, but all share the GES ethos: adventure over pure competition. Signature challenge: The sheer variety—committing to GES means racing Mediterranean forests, African safari lands, volcanic Iceland, and American mountain ranges. No other series delivers this breadth of adventure. Gravel Earth Series represents the soul of gravel racing—adventure, community, and global exploration rather than pure competition. Where Life Time offers production polish and prize money, GES offers riding with giraffes in Kenya, volcanic rifts in Iceland, and Mediterranean forests in Girona. It's 'more of an experience than a competition,' as founder Cristina Freixes puts it. The 2026 consolidation (from 23 to 12 events) and calendar controversies suggest growing pains, but the core experience remains top-tier. Yes if you want adventure beyond typical gravel racing and value experience over prize money. Yes if you're European-based or seeking unique global destinations. Yes if community vibe matters more than production polish. Skip if you need significant prize purses, prefer USA-based racing, or can't handle the travel logistics and expenses.

### SBT GRVL
Tier 1 | Score: 86/100 | 108 mi | 8,189 ft | Steamboat Springs, Colorado | June | gravel
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/steamboat-gravel/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/steamboat-gravel.md

Champagne gravel at altitude with a three-day festival vibe that somehow doesn't ruin the racing. SBT GRVL serves up 108 miles of Colorado's famous 'champagne gravel' - smooth, fast surfaces that seduce you into thinking this will be easy. The 8,189 feet of climbing happens gradually across working ranch land, aspen groves, and sage-covered hills, with 70% gravel that ranges from hero dirt to loose chunky sections that'll humble your bike handling. Signature challenge: The thing nobody tells you about SBT GRVL: champagne gravel is fast until it isn't. The deceptively smooth surfaces let you burn matches early while altitude (course tops out near 8,500ft) and 21 categorized climbs compound every tactical mistake. Riders consistently report feeling it in their power output specifically in the back half, after the Mile 38 cutoff has already sorted the field. If you can hold 20+ mph for five hours at 7,000 feet, the Black course rewards fitness with buttery gravel and legitimate competition. The roughly 10 mph elapsed-average cutoff at Mile 38 sounds generous until you're grinding into headwinds at altitude. Come undertrained and you'll get pulled to the Blue course finish, which isn't the worst fate given the scenery.

It's authentic, community-driven, and legitimately hard. The 'World Championship' name started as a joke but the race earned its reputation through genuine challenge. Yes if you value authenticity, community, and genuine challenge over polish. Yes if you can handle August Midwest heat. Not if you need corporate production value.

Britain's original gravel race where 4,300 meters of climbing meets technical terrain and British weather that doesn't negotiate. The organizer describes it as nearly 100% off-road on hard-packed gravel access roads, with all grades of loose gravel. Dirty Reiver is what happens when you take American gravel ambition and drop it in British conditions. The result is a genuinely hard event that tests fitness, skills, and weather resilience. If you want to understand UK gravel culture, you do Dirty Reiver. Yes, if British gravel interests you. Dirty Reiver is non-negotiable for UK gravel credibility. ### Gravel Locos
Tier 1 | Score: 83/100 | 118 mi | 6,000 ft | Hico, Texas | — | gravel
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/gravel-locos/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/gravel-locos.md

Budget-priced 150-mile Unbound tune-up on gorgeous Texas gravel where Texas heat is the great equalizer. The organizer still publishes only the completed 2025 routes. That year's flagship was 118 miles with approximately 6,000 feet of climbing on open roads with water crossings and a flood backup route. Signature challenge: No current course is published; the last completed flagship was 118 miles with approximately 6,000 feet of gain. Gravel Locos started as a free, charity-donation event and has since grown into a tiered-registration race ($85-$185 depending on distance) — still well under the $250+ entry fees of the destination-gravel circuit. Pros use it as their final rehearsal. Amateurs get to ride with them on gorgeous Texas gravel for a fraction of what Unbound or BWR costs. The catch? Texas heat that can hit 120°F and aid stations that occasionally run dry. Yes if you want a legitimate ultra-gravel experience at a fraction of destination-race entry costs, with international competition and legendary Texas hospitality. Just train for heat.

### The Mid South
Tier 1 | Score: 83/100 | 100 mi | 6,000 ft | Stillwater, Oklahoma | March | gravel
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/mid-south/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/mid-south.md

The early-season gravel race with the biggest heart and the most unpredictable conditions. Fast and tactical when dry. Unrideable mud slog when wet. The weather decides what race you're getting. Signature challenge: The weather lottery. You train for months but Oklahoma decides what race you're riding. The Mid South is what happens when someone builds a gravel race around unreasonable hospitality instead of unreasonable suffering. Bobby Wintle hugs every finisher. The DFL gets the biggest trophy. The community shows up like their lives depend on it. And the weather? The weather does whatever Oklahoma wants. When it's dry, you get a blazing-fast tactical race. When it's wet, you get an unrideable mud nightmare. Either way, you finish to live music, local beer, and a town that genuinely wants you there. This isn't the hardest gravel race. It's not the longest. But it might be the one with the biggest heart. If you value community, celebration, and authentic hospitality over predictable racing conditions—yes, absolutely. If you need to know what you're getting into before you commit—maybe reconsider. The Mid South is chaos wrapped in a Bobby hug. Some years it's fast and perfect. Some years it's a mud disaster. Some years it gets cancelled by wildfires. But the people who come back year after year aren't coming for the course—they're coming for the experience. Show up ready for anything. Leave with stories. Non-negotiables: Weather adaptation training for unpredictable conditions (cold, heat, wind); Red clay handling skills and mud preparation; Wind exposure training on exposed ridgelines

The 125km course through Western Australian forests is brutally technical with 3,200m of climbing on sharp quartz gravel. Grinduro's inaugural European outing trades California dust for Vosges forests, keeping the party-to-pain ratio intact. Enduro format: 4 timed descent stages (technical singletrack), untimed climbs. 62 miles, 6,562 ft. Vosges mountains: steep, forested, technical. Rewards MTB descending, allows social climbing. Signature challenge: Technical singletrack. MTB skills required. Crashes possible. Grinduro France is the French edition of the international festival-race series. Same format as Germany (untimed climbs, 4 timed descents), same party atmosphere (live music, camping, expo), but French: wine instead of beer, Vosges instead of Eifel, French food instead of German. New venue in 2024 (moved to Vosges from Monts du Lyonnais) brings stunning mountain scenery. Most riders prioritize experience over results. Technical descents reward MTB skills but are optional—untimed climbs allow social riding. If you loved Grinduro Germany but prefer French wine and mountain views, this is it. If you can handle 100 kilometers of varied terrain without crying about gravel bike handling, this works. The 2,000 meters of climbing spread across French forest roads won't destroy you, but the mix of surfaces rewards riders who can adapt rather than specialists. ### Gunni Grinder

High-altitude gravel that separates your actual fitness from your sea-level delusions. The organizer-linked 120.5-mile loop gains 9,785 feet, starts near 7,694 feet, averages about 8,754 feet, and reaches about 10,511 feet. Approximately 83% is unpaved, including remote gravel and dirt roads that receive little to no maintenance. Signature challenge: A 120.5-mile loop with 9,785 feet of gain and an average elevation near 8,754 feet. Gunni Grinder is high-altitude mountain gravel done right. This isn't a flat power race—it's a climbing test at thin oxygen. You start at 7,700 ft (already higher than most people live) and max out near 10,000 ft. If you're from low elevation, your FTP will drop 10-15%. Your breathing will be labored. Your bonk will come faster. The Cochetopa Pass Road climb (miles 30-45) is a 15-mile grind that just keeps going—not steep, but relentless at altitude. The high alpine sections (miles 50-70) are exposed, windy, and stunning—above treeline with panoramic Rocky Mountain views. The Razor Creek descent is technical and loose—confidence-testing. Gunnison is a hidden gem: small town, big mountains, zero crowds. The post-race BBQ in the park is low-key awesome—burgers, local beer, live bluegrass. It's not a corporate expo. It's a community celebration. If you can sustain power above 8,000 feet and have low gears for Cochetopa Pass, this is honest mountain suffering without the Leadville circus. Sea-level riders thinking they'll adapt on race day will discover what oxygen debt feels like around mile 40. The terrain isn't technical, but the altitude will expose every fitness gap you've been hiding behind at home.

### Pirinexus 360
Tier 2 | Score: 74/100 | 211 mi | 11,150 ft | Girona, Catalonia, Spain | September | gravel
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/pirinexus-360/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/pirinexus-360.md

The thinking rider's 340k—half the distance of the big ultras but twice as beautiful, with a border-crossing climb that sends half the field home early. The Pirinexus is half smooth greenway cruise, half bike-destroying nightmare. You need 200+ mile legs and 40mm+ tires minimum—the technical border descent after Col d'Ares will put narrower rubber on foot. This isn't a watts contest; it's navigation, bike handling, and knowing when to push through the Pyrenean climbs versus when to survive them. Show up undertrained and that 18-hour cutoff becomes very real very fast.

### Southern Cross Gravel
Tier 2 | Score: 71/100 | 50 mi | 5,500 ft | Dahlonega, Georgia | March | gravel

Signature challenge: One aid station, visited twice: 50mi riders must clear Winding Stair Gap (mile 12) by 12:30 PM or get redirected onto the 30mi course back to Montaluce Winery. It's the only gravel race where you might actually want to stay at the finish line longer than it took to ride the race. The course is honest suffering—no gimmicks, just real North Georgia topography. If you're a diesel engine who thrives on sustained power, this will hurt. If you're a punchy climber who can recover on descents, you'll love it. If you can handle 6,200 feet of punchy Georgia climbs over 50 miles and aren't fazed by potential mud lottery conditions, this delivers solid suffering with the best post-race scene in the Southeast. Highlands Gravel Classic is one of the US qualifiers for UCI Gravel World Championships (alongside Big Sugar and Mammoth TUFF)—that alone makes it significant. The race itself is a 67-mile smashfest through chunky Ozark gravel with constant climbs and technical descents (a 53-mile/3,700ft Masters course covers the official 60+/50+ age-band distance). It's short enough to race hard and long enough to hurt. For anyone chasing UCI qualification, this is a strong option. Yes if you're chasing UCI qualification. Yes if you want a short, intense race on technical terrain. Skip if you want ultra-endurance or smooth gravel.

The Crystal Bear is an overnight point-to-point bikepacking odyssey through the Northwoods of Wisconsin and Michigan's Upper Peninsula. Unlike mass-start gravel races, this is self-supported adventure racing: you carry overnight gear, navigate independently, and resupply at small-town gas stations 40-60 miles apart. This isn't about crushing segments or chasing KOMs. It's about holding it together mentally and physically for 15-30 hours straight while entirely self-reliant. Signature challenge: Managing 8-10 hours of solo darkness riding through remote Northwoods forest while fighting sleep deprivation, cold, and psychological isolation with zero external support. The Crystal Bear isn't about who's fastest. It's about who can hold it together when every external factor—darkness, cold, loneliness, sleep deprivation—is screaming to quit. This is overnight bikepacking racing at its purest: 192 miles of self-supported Northwoods gravel where you'll spend 8-10 hours riding solo through pitch-black forest with nothing but your headlight and your own thoughts. The terrain itself isn't brutal—8,000 feet over 192 miles is moderate climbing—but the format is the challenge. You'll fight sandy sections that kill momentum. You'll navigate stream crossings at 2 AM when your brain is mush. You'll stop to eat and start shivering within 5 minutes from overnight cold. And you'll do it all alone, with resupply points 40-60 miles apart and spotty cell service. This isn't a race for your first ultra-endurance event. It's for riders who've done the long stuff and are ready to test themselves against isolation and darkness. If you finish, you'll have earned something real. If you DNF, you'll learn exactly where your mental limits are. Either way, you won't forget it. You need overnight riding experience and the gear to match—this isn't your first gravel race with a bivy thrown in last minute. The sandy Wisconsin forest roads will humble roadie legs, and navigation errors in darkness can add hours. Come if you've done multi-day rides solo and understand that 'self-supported' means exactly that when you're flat-tired at 2 AM in the middle of nowhere.

Iowa Wind and Rock is 340 miles of honest Iowa gravel: crushed limestone roads rolling through endless agricultural land with zero shelter from wind. Iowa Wind and Rock is 340 miles of truth serum on gravel. You can't hide behind teammates, tactics, or short bursts of power. This is 30-50 hours of continuous forward motion where the wind grinds you down, the constant rolling terrain never lets you recover, and your own brain becomes the biggest obstacle. The terrain itself isn't hard—Iowa gravel is fast when dry, and there are no mountains. But the wind is relentless. You'll spend hours grinding into headwinds at 8-10 mph, watching your finish time balloon, questioning why you signed up. Sleep deprivation hits around Hour 25-30. Navigation errors happen. The loneliness of self-supported racing amplifies every doubt. And April weather is a lottery: rain turns the course into mud hell, cold overnight temps test your layering strategy, or you luck out with mild sunny conditions. Either outcome teaches you something. You need 200+ mile experience and the mental fortitude to grind through 40+ hours of constant wind exposure across endless farm roads. This isn't about watts—it's about navigation skills, self-sufficiency, and accepting that you'll question every life choice around Mile 200. Skip it if you've never done overnight riding or think Iowa looks flat and easy.

USA Cycling Gravel Nationals delivers what the name promises—a legitimate national championship with open entry and UCI Worlds qualification. ### Boulder Roubaix Road Race
Tier 2 | Score: 61/100 | 30 mi | 1,200 ft | Boulder Reservoir, Boulder County, Colorado, USA | April | gravel
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/boulder-roubaix/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/boulder-roubaix.md

Colorado's 34-year spring classic. 61% dirt, USAC-sanctioned, and unapologetically hard. Rolling mixed-surface through North Boulder County agricultural landscape. The 2026 course is a new 30-mile (48 km) loop — 61% unpaved, 39% paved — that starts and finishes at Boulder Reservoir. The terrain is constant undulation through working farm and county roads that can be anywhere from smooth to extremely rutted depending on weather. No single dramatic climb, but the accumulated rolling and the wind across open terrain create a war of attrition. The finishing stretch along the Boulder Feeder Canal and across the reservoir dams adds a challenging technical element to the final miles. Signature challenge: The wind. Not the terrain, not the climbing, not the distance — the wind across open North Boulder County farmland is what defines Boulder Roubaix. In 2024, it shut down the race. On any given edition, it determines whether the dirt roads are fast-rolling or soul-crushing. Combined with the unpredictable surface conditions and spring weather variability, the wind transforms a rolling 30-mile circuit into a legitimate test of tactical racing and survival. Boulder Roubaix is what happens when you take the spirit of Paris-Roubaix and transplant it to Colorado's Front Range farm roads. Since 1992, this biennial race has sent riders onto the unpaved county roads north of Boulder — roads that were 'gravel' decades before gravel became a category. The course does not need cobblestones to create chaos: rutted dirt roads, spring wind that can shut down the race, and surface conditions that change hourly deliver the unpredictability that defines a classic. It is a proper USAC road race with categorized fields and a pro purse, not a recreational ride. The 2026 edition moves to Boulder Reservoir with a new 30-mile loop that is 61% unpaved — further embracing the mixed-surface identity that has always defined this event. Yes if you are a competitive road or gravel racer who wants a legitimate USAC road race on mixed surfaces. Yes if you live in Colorado and want to test your early-season form on the defining spring race. Yes if you want to experience the event that was doing 'gravel racing' before the term existed. Skip if you want a long-distance endurance challenge (most categories are 30-60 miles), or if you need a destination event with a national profile. Non-negotiables: Mixed-surface tire selection tested on dirt roads; Wind-exposure training on open terrain; Self-sufficiency kit: pump, spare tube, multi-tool

### Finnish Gravel
Tier 2 | Score: 61/100 | 110 mi | 2,129 ft | Lahti, Paijanne Tavastia, Finland | August | gravel
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/finnish-gravel/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/finnish-gravel.md

F1 glamour meets Nordic gravel in a UNESCO Geopark—premium experience, premium price tag, unique bucket-list appeal. Fast, flowing Finnish gravel through UNESCO Geopark terrain. Well-maintained gravel roads, lakeside routes, and Nordic ski paths create a high-speed experience rather than a technical challenge. The continuous undulations and steep kickers separate riders, but this is racing, not survival. Riders average 35 kph on the twisting ski path sections. Signature challenge: Not one killer climb, but the relentless accumulation of steep kickers and undulations that 'will separate' riders. Plus the bugs at every stop. FNLD GRVL is what happens when an F1 driver falls in love with gravel. It's not the most challenging course or the deepest pro field, but for a unique Nordic cultural experience wrapped in top-tier event production, it delivers. The midnight sun, the UNESCO Geopark, the Finnish hospitality, and the SBT GRVL pedigree create something genuinely special. Yes if you want a unique Nordic cultural experience with top-tier event production. Yes if you're an F1/Bottas fan. Skip if you're chasing big climbing or watching your budget. International travelers should weigh the high costs against the unique experience.

A well-organized, scenic road cycling celebration of Alberta's badlands landscape that delivers excellent value and community atmosphere for riders of all abilities seeking a memorable weekend adventure. ### THE EQUALIZER - Missouri State Championship
Tier 2 | Score: 60/100 | 62 mi | 3,786 ft | Marthasville, Missouri | November | gravel
Profile: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/the-equalizer/
Markdown: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/the-equalizer.md

Missouri's state championship is a cold-morning rollers grind through wine country that finds out whose fitness survived the fall. Rolling Missouri River Valley terrain. Roughly 3,800 ft over 62 miles = constant ups and downs, no sustained climbs. Mix of smooth gravel county roads (85%) and paved connectors (15%). Terrain is rolling but not extreme. Cold November mornings and late-season fitness are the defining challenge. Signature challenge: The constant rollers, not one single climb. 3,800 feet arrives in dozens of short punches with no flat mile to recover on, and by November most of the field is riding on fading late-season fitness. THE EQUALIZER is Missouri's state gravel championship--62 miles through wine country on the first Saturday of November. The course is rolling but not brutal (3,786 ft, constant ups and downs, no mountain climbs). The challenge is cold-start pacing and late-season fitness, not heat: mornings are cold, daylight is short, and most of the field hasn't raced hard since summer. The wine country setting is scenic, and Missouri gravel is smooth compared to mountain states. State championship brings some fast racers, but the field is mostly recreational (200-300 riders). St. Louis airport is about an hour away, making travel easy. Marthasville is small, but nearby St. Charles has lodging. This is an emerging Midwest gravel scene event--not iconic, but solid. If you can handle 95°F with 80% humidity while grinding constant rollers for six hours, this is solid Midwest racing. The course won't break you—smooth gravel, manageable elevation—but November cold will punish anyone who shows up dressed for September. Perfect for riders wanting state championship bragging rights without the technical demands of mountain races.

## Data Schema

Each race profile (JSON) contains:
- `race.name`, `race.slug`, `race.tagline`
- `race.vitals`: distance_mi, elevation_ft, location, date, terrain_types, field_size
- `race.gravel_god_rating`: overall_score, tier, 14 dimension scores, discipline
- `race.course_description`: character, suffering_zones, signature_challenge
- `race.terrain`: primary, surface, technical_rating, features
- `race.climate`: primary, description, challenges
- `race.logistics`: airport, lodging_strategy, official_site
- `race.history`: founded, origin_story, notable_moments
- `race.final_verdict`: one_liner, should_you_race, alternatives
- `race.non_negotiables`: training requirements with deadlines
- `race.citations`: source URLs
- `race.tire_recommendations`: primary tires, pressure tables

Access individual profiles at: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race/{slug}/
Machine-readable JSON index: https://gravelgodcycling.com/race-index.json
REST API: https://gravelgodcycling.com/api/v1/docs
